title: The Boring Fund
intro: A text from your bank about your monthly investment. After all those promises of fast riches, a plain one feels odd.
But some messages are real. Mirage loves it when you stop trusting the honest ones.

screen.context: Last year you set up a small monthly investment in a plain index fund, yourself, in the Orrin app.

msg.text: Investments can go down as well as up.
See your holdings in the Orrin app.
You do not need to do anything.

sender.label: Same thread as your bank texts
sender.lens: It sits with your past bank messages.
sender.why: A name proves little. What it asks matters.

plan.label: A plan you set up
plan.lens: A small monthly amount you chose yourself.

fund.label: A plain fund
fund.lens: An ordinary index fund, no secret.

risk.label: A risk warning
risk.lens: It says investments can go down as well as up.

app.label: Look in your own app
app.lens: It sends you to your own app.
app.why: Pointing you to your own app is honest.

nothing.label: Asks for nothing
nothing.why: A message that asks for nothing is usually honest.

actions.label: Check my holdings in the Orrin app myself

go_ahead.line: The app showed the £50 had been added to your fund, as planned. Nothing unusual, and nothing to fear.

ignore.line: Nothing bad happened. A quick look in the app would have confirmed the plan was working.

block_report.line: That was your own monthly plan. When every message looks like a scam, you stop trusting your own choices.
block_report.mirageSays: If you trust nothing, I win anyway.

what_if.block_report: It matched a plan you made, warned about risk, asked for nothing and sent you to your own app. Boring and honest.
what_if.ignore: Ignoring was safe. Recognising a real message is the skill: it asks for nothing secret and matches something you know.

golden_rule: A plain, boring plan you set up yourself, with a risk warning and nothing to give, is usually honest. Check in your own app.

quick_check.q: What made this investment text honest?

options.text: It matched a plan you set up, warned about risk and asked for nothing

quick_check.explain: No promises, a risk warning and nothing asked are the real signs.

hints.nudge: What is this message actually asking you to do?

rows.k: Same thread as your bank texts
